question.prompt: Why did the deckhand most likely wave sharply at the captain after Tomas shouted?

stimulus.title: The Last Ferry
stimulus.body: Tomas sprinted down the pier, his backpack thumping against his spine like an impatient drum. The ferry's horn had already sounded twice, and its gangway was folding upward with the slow, deliberate finality of a closing book. 'Wait!' he shouted, though his voice was swallowed by the wind rolling off the harbour. A deckhand glanced up, hesitated, then waved sharply at the captain. The gangway paused, hovering halfway, before creaking back down just long enough for Tomas to leap aboard, stumbling onto the deck as the ferry's engines rumbled to life beneath his feet. He caught his breath against the railing, watching the pier and its silent, indifferent clock tower shrink slowly into the grey afternoon.

options.text: To signal the captain to briefly reopen the gangway so Tomas could still board.
To warn the captain that the ferry was in danger of sinking.
To tell the captain that Tomas was not permitted onto the ferry.
To greet Tomas, who was an old friend of the deckhand.

question.explanation: Immediately after the deckhand waves, the text describes the gangway pausing and creaking back down 'just long enough for Tomas to leap aboard.' This close sequence of events shows the wave directly caused the gangway to reopen briefly. Nothing in the passage suggests any danger to the ferry, so a warning about sinking does not fit. There is also no mention of the deckhand and Tomas knowing each other, ruling out a friendly greeting as the reason for the wave.
